$comment: Committed, project-scoped rules only. Machine-local overrides go in .claude/settings.local.json, which is gitignored.

allow names exact commands, never `uv *` or `git *`: `uv run` executes whatever follows it, so a broad rule would auto-approve `uv run rm -rf .` past every deny rule. Read-only git needs no rule; Claude Code already runs it without asking. `uv add`, `git push` and anything else unlisted still prompt.
Read(!.env.example) carves the committed contract back out of Read(.env.*). An allow rule couldn't, because deny always wins.
Deny rules are guardrails, not a boundary: they miss `bash -c`, absolute paths and scripts that open files themselves. For enforcement, turn on the sandbox with /sandbox (macOS, Linux, WSL2).
